item.text:
## Summary

Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Fix the timestamp contract before merge because a process whose latest event is `started` is reported as finished.

## Changes

The process model adds `finished_at` to its latest-event row for each process. The schema catalog documents the column and its null behavior.

## Critical

- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — Align `finished_at` with the event it measures — For process 20, whose only event is `started`, the model returns the start time as `finished_at`. The source allows `created`, `started`, and `cleared` and defines no explicit completion event. — Consumers using `finished_at` to count completions will count processes whose latest event only records a start. — Fix: Name the column `started_at` if it represents starts, or derive it from a source event that records completion.

## Important

- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — Document why a previously started process returns NULL — Process 30 returns NULL after its `started` event is followed by `cleared`. The catalog says “NULL means the process has never been started,” while the model uses `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end` on the latest event. — Consumers following the catalog will classify previously started processes as never started after a clear event.

## Suggestions

- models/schema.yml:12 — comments — Qualify the UTC guarantee — A latest `started` event with `occurred_at = '2026-01-01T01:00:00+01:00'` retains the `+01:00` offset. The catalog says “Stored in UTC using the source event timestamp,” while `then occurred_at` returns the source text directly. — Consumers sorting the advertised UTC strings can misorder events when source records use different offsets.
- models/processes.sql:10 — tests — Cover the timestamp for a created-only process — The source fixture includes process 10 with only a `created` event, and no model test asserts that this input returns NULL for the new timestamp. — A regression that assigns timestamps to created-only processes has no test assertion to catch it.
